description: This topic explains the meaning, modes and means of transport and communication, the factors influencing transport routes, their importance to development and trade, and the networks and problems of transport and communication in Tanzania and East Africa.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best describes the difference between transport and communication?

options.text: Transport moves people and goods, while communication moves information and messages
Transport moves only goods, while communication moves only people
Transport and communication mean exactly the same thing
Communication moves goods, while transport moves messages

mcq.explanation: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another, while communication is the passing of information, ideas and messages between people.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is most suitable for carrying crude oil over long distances on land?

options.text: Air transport
Pipeline transport
Road transport
Railway transport

mcq.explanation: Pipelines are designed to move liquids and gases such as oil and water cheaply and continuously over long distances on land, for example the East African Crude Oil Pipeline.

mcq.questionText: The TAZARA railway line links Tanzania with which neighbouring country?

options.text: Kenya
Uganda
Zambia
Mozambique

mcq.explanation: The Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority (TAZARA) line runs from Dar es Salaam to Kapiri Mposhi in Zambia, giving landlocked Zambia access to the sea.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the busiest and largest seaport in Tanzania?

options.text: Tanga
Mtwara
Dar es Salaam
Bagamoyo

mcq.explanation: The port of Dar es Salaam handles the largest volume of cargo in Tanzania and serves several landlocked countries in the region.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of transport is the fastest for moving people and light goods over very long distances?

options.text: Air transport
Water transport
Railway transport
Road transport

mcq.explanation: Air transport is the fastest means of moving passengers and perishable or light valuable goods over long distances, although it is the most expensive.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of water transport on inland waters in Tanzania?

options.text: Ships sailing in the Indian Ocean
Ferries crossing Lake Victoria
Aircraft landing at Mwanza
Lorries on the Dar-Mwanza road

mcq.explanation: Inland water transport uses lakes and rivers; ferries and steamers on Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika and Lake Nyasa are good examples in Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which factor would MOST likely raise the cost of building a road across a region?

options.text: Flat, gently sloping land
A dry, stable climate
Rugged, mountainous relief with many rivers
A densely populated trading area

mcq.explanation: Steep slopes, mountains and many rivers require expensive bridges, tunnels and earthworks, greatly increasing the cost of constructing transport routes.

mcq.questionText: Which is a major advantage of railway transport over road transport?

options.text: It can reach every village and home directly
It carries bulky and heavy goods cheaply over long distances
It is the cheapest to construct
It is faster than air transport

mcq.explanation: Railways can pull many wagons at once, making them very economical for transporting bulky and heavy goods such as minerals and cement over long distances.

mcq.questionText: Which means of communication allows two people to talk to each other instantly even when far apart?

options.text: Newspaper
Telephone
Postal letter
Notice board

mcq.explanation: The telephone, especially the mobile phone, allows two-way instant voice communication between people who are far apart.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a disadvantage of road transport?

options.text: It cannot reach rural areas
It is unsuitable for short distances
It suffers from traffic jams and frequent accidents
It cannot carry passengers

mcq.explanation: Road transport is flexible and reaches many places, but it is affected by traffic congestion, accidents and high maintenance costs of roads and vehicles.

mcq.questionText: The central railway line in Tanzania mainly connects Dar es Salaam to which town on Lake Tanganyika?

options.text: Mwanza
Kigoma
Arusha
Mbeya

mcq.explanation: The central railway line runs from Dar es Salaam through Dodoma and Tabora to Kigoma on Lake Tanganyika, with a branch to Mwanza on Lake Victoria.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best explains the importance of transport and communication to trade?

options.text: They make goods and market information move easily between buyers and sellers
They reduce the population of trading towns
They stop people from selling surplus produce
They make all goods free of charge

mcq.explanation: Good transport moves goods to markets while communication spreads price and market information, encouraging both internal and international trade.

mcq.questionText: A transport corridor such as the Central Corridor is best described as:

options.text: A single tarmac road in a city centre
A route linking a port to inland and landlocked countries using several transport modes
A footpath used only by tourists
An airport runway for international flights

mcq.explanation: A corridor links a seaport to interior regions and landlocked neighbours using roads, railways and pipelines; the Central Corridor serves Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and the DRC through Dar es Salaam.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common problem facing transport in many developing countries?

options.text: Too many modern airports
Poor and badly maintained roads and few railway lines
Excessive government funding for transport
Too many trained engineers

mcq.explanation: Developing countries often face poor road conditions, limited railway networks, shortage of funds and inadequate maintenance, which slow down transport.

mcq.questionText: The internet has improved communication mainly because it:

options.text: Can only be used to send paper letters
Allows fast sharing of information, e-mail and online services worldwide
Works only inside one country
Replaces the need for any electricity

mcq.explanation: The internet enables rapid worldwide exchange of information through e-mail, websites, mobile money and social media, supporting trade, education and services.

fib.questionText: The movement of people and goods from one place to another is called _____.
fib.explanation: Transport refers to carrying people and goods from one place to another using different modes such as road, rail, water and air.

fib.questionText: The passing of information, ideas and messages between people is called _____.
fib.explanation: Communication is the process of sending and receiving information through means such as telephone, internet, radio and newspapers.

fib.questionText: The railway line that connects Dar es Salaam to Kapiri Mposhi in Zambia is known as the _____ railway.
fib.explanation: TAZARA (Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority) gives landlocked Zambia access to the sea through the port of Dar es Salaam.

fib.questionText: The mode of transport that uses pipes to carry oil, gas and water is called _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Pipeline transport moves liquids and gases continuously and cheaply over long distances on land.

fib.questionText: Transport that uses lakes and rivers within a country is called _____ water transport.
fib.explanation: Inland water transport uses lakes such as Victoria and Tanganyika and rivers, while marine transport uses oceans and seas.

fib.questionText: The fastest but most expensive mode of transport is _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Air transport is very fast and suitable for long distances and perishable goods, but it has high costs.

fib.questionText: The seaport located in the southern coast of Tanzania near the natural gas fields is _____.
fib.explanation: Mtwara port serves the southern regions of Tanzania and is associated with the natural gas industry of the area.

fib.questionText: A landform feature such as mountains and steep slopes that affects the building of roads is called _____.
fib.explanation: Relief refers to the shape of the land; rugged relief makes route construction difficult and expensive.

fib.questionText: The branch of the central railway line that ends at a town on Lake Victoria reaches _____.
fib.explanation: A branch of the central line goes to Mwanza on Lake Victoria, linking it with ferry services on the lake.

fib.questionText: Sending letters and parcels through post offices is part of _____ communication.
fib.explanation: Postal communication involves the delivery of letters and parcels through the post office network.

tf.questionText: Transport and communication mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Transport moves people and goods, while communication moves information and messages; they are related but different.

tf.questionText: Air transport is generally the most expensive mode of transport.
tf.explanation: Air transport has high fuel, aircraft and airport costs, making it the most expensive mode despite being the fastest.

tf.questionText: Pipeline transport is well suited for carrying solid goods such as bags of cement.
tf.explanation: Pipelines carry liquids and gases such as oil, gas and water, not solid goods.

tf.questionText: The port of Dar es Salaam also serves landlocked countries in the region.
tf.explanation: Dar es Salaam port serves countries such as Zambia, the DRC, Rwanda, Burundi and Malawi through corridors and railways.

tf.questionText: Rugged relief and many rivers make the construction of transport routes cheaper.
tf.explanation: Rugged relief and rivers require costly bridges, tunnels and earthworks, making route construction more expensive, not cheaper.

tf.questionText: Railway transport is suitable for carrying bulky and heavy goods over long distances.
tf.explanation: Railways can haul many wagons at once, making them economical for heavy and bulky goods such as minerals and grain.

tf.questionText: Good transport and communication discourage trade and economic development.
tf.explanation: Good transport and communication promote trade and development by moving goods, people and information efficiently.

tf.questionText: Mobile phones and the internet have greatly improved communication in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Mobile phones, mobile money and the internet have spread quickly, improving access to information and services across Tanzania.

tf.questionText: A transport corridor uses only one mode of transport from the coast to the interior.
tf.explanation: A corridor usually combines several modes such as roads, railways and pipelines to link a port with inland and landlocked areas.

tf.questionText: Shortage of funds and poor maintenance are common transport problems in developing countries.
tf.explanation: Many developing countries lack enough money to build and maintain roads, railways and ports, leading to poor transport services.

summary.correctAnswer: Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another, while communication is the passing of information, ideas and messages between people.
summary.explanation: These definitions show that transport deals with physical movement while communication deals with the exchange of information.

summary.questionText: List the main modes of transport.
summary.correctAnswer: Road, railway, water (inland and marine), air and pipeline transport.
summary.explanation: These are the major modes used to move people and goods on land, water and in the air.

summary.questionText: State two advantages of road transport.
summary.correctAnswer: It is flexible and reaches many places including villages, and it is convenient for short distances and door-to-door delivery.
summary.explanation: Road transport connects rural and urban areas and links easily with other modes, making it widely used.

summary.questionText: Give two advantages of railway transport.
summary.correctAnswer: It carries bulky and heavy goods cheaply over long distances, and it is relatively safe with fewer accidents than roads.
summary.explanation: Railways are economical for large loads and reduce road congestion and accidents.

summary.correctAnswer: Postal services, telephone or mobile phone, internet, radio, television and newspapers.
summary.explanation: These means carry information to individuals and to the public over short and long distances.

summary.questionText: State three factors that influence the development of transport routes.
summary.correctAnswer: Relief, climate, cost of construction, population density and economic activities.
summary.explanation: Routes are built where the land is suitable, costs are affordable and there is demand from people and economic activities.

summary.questionText: Name two important seaports in Tanzania.
summary.explanation: These ports handle imports and exports and link Tanzania to international trade and to landlocked neighbours.

summary.questionText: Explain the importance of transport and communication to development.
summary.correctAnswer: They move goods, people and information, promote trade, create jobs, open up remote areas and support agriculture, industry and services.
summary.explanation: Efficient transport and communication are key to economic growth and the linking of regions.

summary.questionText: Identify two problems facing transport and communication in developing countries.
summary.correctAnswer: Poor and few roads or railways, shortage of funds, poor maintenance, rugged relief and limited skilled personnel.
summary.explanation: These problems reduce the quality and reach of transport and communication services.

summary.questionText: Suggest two solutions to transport and communication problems in developing countries.
summary.correctAnswer: Increase funding and investment, build and maintain better roads, railways and ports, train skilled workers and expand mobile and internet networks.
summary.explanation: Investment, maintenance, training and modern technology improve the efficiency of transport and communication.

hoq.questionText: A mining company in central Tanzania needs to move large amounts of heavy minerals to the port of Dar es Salaam for export at the lowest possible cost. Which mode of transport should it mainly use and why?

options.text: Air transport, because it is the fastest
Railway transport, because it carries bulky and heavy goods cheaply over long distances
Pipeline transport, because minerals flow easily through pipes
Air transport, because minerals are perishable

hoq.explanation: Heavy bulky minerals are best moved by railway, such as the central line, because trains haul large loads cheaply over long distances; pipelines only carry liquids and gases.

hoq.questionText: A region with steep mountains, heavy rainfall and a small scattered population has very few roads. Which combination of factors best explains this poor transport development?

options.text: Flat relief, dry climate and dense population
Rugged relief, harsh climate and low population reducing demand and raising costs
Cheap construction and high government funding
Many economic activities and large markets

hoq.explanation: Steep relief and heavy rainfall raise construction and maintenance costs, while a small scattered population gives little demand, so few roads are built.

hoq.questionText: Landlocked countries such as Zambia, Rwanda and Burundi rely heavily on Tanzanian ports and corridors. What does this BEST show about transport and communication?

options.text: Landlocked countries do not need transport at all
Transport routes and corridors link countries and promote regional trade and cooperation
Ports are useful only to the country that owns them
Air transport is the only option for landlocked countries

hoq.explanation: Corridors and ports such as Dar es Salaam connect landlocked neighbours to the sea, showing how transport networks promote regional trade, integration and development.
